steps.title: Import required Node.js modules
steps.instruction: Import the http module and the EventEmitter class from the events module.
steps.hint: Use the require() function to import Node.js core modules. The http module is needed to create an HTTP server, and EventEmitter from events will help manage SSE connections.
steps.seedCode: // Import the http module and EventEmitter from events
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have the http module and EventEmitter class imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: The http module and EventEmitter class from the events module are imported using require().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the required Node.js modules. The http module will allow you to create an HTTP server, and EventEmitter will help manage real-time connections for SSE.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both modules: http and EventEmitter from events. Check that you're using the correct require() syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Remember to use require() to import the http module and EventEmitter from the events module.

steps.title: Create an HTTP server instance
steps.instruction: Create an HTTP server using http.createServer() and store it in a variable named 'server'.
steps.hint: Use the createServer method from the imported http module to create a server instance.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a basic HTTP server
const server = http.createServer();
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a server variable ready to handle incoming HTTP requests.
successCriteria: A server variable is created using http.createServer()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created an HTTP server instance.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using http.createServer() and storing it in a variable named 'server'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server instance wasn't created correctly. Check that you're using the imported http module and the createServer method.

steps.title: Initialize an EventEmitter for broadcasting
steps.instruction: Create a new EventEmitter instance and assign it to a constant variable named 'eventEmitter'.
steps.hint: Use the 'new' keyword with EventEmitter to create an instance. Store it in a variable so you can use it later.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating an EventEmitter instance
const myEmitter = new EventEmitter();
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have an EventEmitter instance ready to broadcast events to connected clients.
successCriteria: A constant variable named 'eventEmitter' is declared and assigned a new EventEmitter instance.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created an EventEmitter instance that will serve as the central event system for broadcasting messages.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're creating a new EventEmitter instance and storing it in a variable named 'eventEmitter'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using the correct syntax to create an EventEmitter instance and assigning it to a variable named 'eventEmitter'.

steps.title: Set up the server request handler
steps.instruction: Add a request handler function to the server that checks the request URL and method.
steps.hint: Create a function that takes request and response parameters, then logs or inspects the URL.
steps.expectedOutcome: A request handler function is defined and ready to be attached to the server.
successCriteria: A function named requestHandler (or similar) is created that accepts req and res parameters and checks req.url.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the request handler function. Next, we'll attach it to the server.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the function, but make sure it accepts both req and res parameters and logs or checks the URL.
steps.feedbackWrong: The request handler function is missing or incomplete. Create a function that handles incoming requests.

steps.title: Configure SSE response headers
steps.instruction: Inside your request handler function, set the response headers for Server-Sent Events when the request URL is '/events'.
steps.hint: Use res.writeHead() with status 200 and headers: 'Content-Type' as 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control' as 'no-cache', and 'Connection' as 'keep-alive'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The request handler will now properly configure HTTP headers for SSE connections when clients access the '/events' endpoint.
successCriteria: The request handler sets status 200 and includes 'Content-Type', 'Cache-Control', and 'Connection' headers for SSE when req.url is '/events'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've correctly configured the SSE response headers. This ensures the client receives a proper event stream connection.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you're setting all three required headers: Content-Type, Cache-Control, and Connection.
steps.feedbackWrong: The headers aren't properly configured. Make sure to use res.writeHead() with status 200 and the correct header values for SSE.

steps.title: Establish the SSE connection
steps.instruction: Inside the requestHandler function, write the code to send the initial SSE response that establishes the connection and keeps it open.
steps.hint: You need to write the initial SSE data format and keep the connection alive. Use res.write() to send the initial data.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will send the initial SSE data format when a client connects to the /events endpoint, establishing the SSE connection.
successCriteria: The requestHandler function sends the initial SSE data using res.write() with the proper SSE format.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully written the initial SSE response to establish the connection.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using res.write() with the proper SSE data format (e.g., 'data: ...\n\n').
steps.feedbackWrong: The initial SSE response wasn't properly written. Check the SSE format and ensure you're using res.write() inside the correct conditional block.

steps.title: Create event listener for updates
steps.instruction: Inside the requestHandler function, add an event listener to the eventEmitter that sends data to the SSE client when updates occur.
steps.hint: Use eventEmitter.on() to listen for a specific event name, then write the data to the response using res.write() with the proper SSE format.
steps.expectedOutcome: The requestHandler will now listen for broadcast events and send them to connected SSE clients.
successCriteria: An event listener is added inside the requestHandler that uses eventEmitter.on() and writes data to the response with res.write().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added an event listener that will send updates to SSE clients.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using eventEmitter.on() inside the requestHandler and writing data with res.write().
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the code: you need to add an event listener inside the requestHandler function that listens for events and writes data to the response.

steps.title: Handle client disconnection
steps.instruction: Inside the requestHandler function, add a response close handler to remove the event listener when the SSE connection ends.
steps.hint: You can listen for the 'close' event on the response object and inside that event handler, call eventEmitter.removeListener() with the same listener function you created in step 7.
steps.expectedOutcome: The SSE endpoint will properly clean up event listeners when clients disconnect, preventing memory leaks.
successCriteria: The requestHandler function includes a response close handler that removes the update event listener when the connection closes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a close handler to clean up resources when clients disconnect from the SSE stream.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're listening for the 'close' event on the response object and removing the exact same listener function that was added for updates.
steps.feedbackWrong: The close handler is missing or incorrect. Remember to add res.on('close', ...) and call eventEmitter.removeListener() inside it.

steps.title: Start the server
steps.instruction: Make the server listen on port 3000 and log a startup message when it's ready.
steps.hint: Use the server.listen() method with the port number and a callback function that logs a message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will be configured to listen for incoming connections on port 3000 and log a confirmation message when started.
successCriteria: The server.listen() method is called with port 3000 and a callback function that logs a startup message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully started the server on port 3000 with a startup log message.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling server.listen() with both the port number and a callback function that logs a message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't properly configured to listen. Check that you're using server.listen() with port 3000 and a callback.

steps.title: Test the SSE endpoint
steps.instruction: Start the server by calling server.listen() on port 3000 and add a console.log to confirm it's running.
steps.hint: Use server.listen(3000, () => { console.log('Server listening on port 3000'); }) to start the server and log a message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will start and log a confirmation message to the console.
successCriteria: The server is started with server.listen() on port 3000 and logs a message to the console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The server is now running and ready to accept SSE connections.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the server, but make sure to include a console.log message to confirm it's running.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've called server.listen() with the correct port and added a console.log inside the callback.
